# Zeront - Vulnerability Radar by SecuScan

Zeront tracks vulnerabilities that are confirmed exploited in the wild
(CISA KEV catalog) plus flaws SecuScan is actively tracking in Vietnam with
real aggregate scan data. Updated daily. Data policy: aggregates only -
individual websites are never named or scored in public data.

## Machine-readable endpoints

- Radar page (human): https://secuscan.dannyphan.me/radar/
- JSON feed (schema zeront-feed/2): https://secuscan.dannyphan.me/radar/feed.json
- JSON feed (mirror): https://dankezo.github.io/zeront/feed.json
- RSS 2.0 feed: https://secuscan.dannyphan.me/radar/feed.xml
- Browser extension (checks the user's own sites against the feed):
  https://github.com/dankezo/zeront/releases
- Source repository: https://github.com/dankezo/zeront

## Feed schema (zeront-feed/2)

Top level: generated_at, stats (sites_tracked_vn, warnings_sent,
kev_total, kev_new_this_week), featured[], kev_recent[], sources[].

featured[] - flaws tracked in Vietnam from SecuScan's own scans:
  id, cves[], severity, title_vi/title_en, affected_vi/affected_en
  (affected software + version range), fix_vi/fix_en, vn_affected
  (confirmed affected site count in Vietnam, aggregate), tracked_since,
  match { type: "server-version" | "page-signal", ... } - detection rules
  the Zeront extension uses to check a user's own site.

kev_recent[] - newest CISA KEV entries (last 21 days, max 25):
  cve, vendor, product, name, added, due (CISA remediation due date),
  due_in_days (days until due, negative = overdue, computed at build),
  ransomware ("Known" | "Unknown"), desc (CISA short description, EN),
  impact_vi / impact_en (short plain-language consequence label),
  plain_vi (1-2 sentence Vietnamese plain-language explanation of where
  the flaw is and what an attacker gains; may be null), link (CVE record).

## How an agent should use this

1. Fetch feed.json (mirror as fallback).
2. Fingerprint the user's site (server header, CMS/framework signals,
   package versions when source access is granted).
3. Match against featured[].match rules first (highest confidence),
   then kev_recent by vendor/product.
4. Report matches in plain language with impact_vi/plain_vi, the fix,
   and the CISA due date. Re-check daily.
